column1: # regeln/INVARIANTEN.tsv - the core invariants an update must not silently break.
# ONE OWNER: bin/fm-update-guard-lib.sh (fm_update_guard) is the only reader and
# the only owner of this file's format. Nothing else parses it; a second reader
# would make this list two lists.
# WHY: an update is a fast-forward of tracked files, so a commit that deletes a
# gate, drops a hook registration, or removes the rule database lands as quietly
# as a typo fix and disarms the fleet without a single refusal. This list is the
# short answer to "what must still be there after the advance"; the guard checks
# it inside a throwaway worktree of the TARGET commit, before the home moves.
# FORMAT: one row per invariant, tab-separated, comments and blank lines ignored:
#   <art>\t<ziel>\t<beschreibung>
#   art = pfad    <ziel> is a repo-relative path that must EXIST at the target
#                 commit (a data file: rulebook, config, package definition).
#   art = exec    <ziel> is a repo-relative tool that must exist AND be runnable
#                 at the target commit. Runnable is read per call convention:
#                 a *-lib.sh is sourced by its callers, so it must parse clean
#                 (bash -n); every other exec target must additionally carry the
#                 executable bit, because its callers invoke it as a program.
#   art = hook    <ziel> is "<event>:<script-basename>" and must appear as a
#                 registered hook command for <event> in the target commit's
#                 .claude/settings.json (read with jq, matched on the basename).
#   art = golden  <ziel> is a golden-suite fixture that must exist at the target
#                 commit. TRANSITION: a missing golden target is a WARNING, not a
#                 refusal, until the file lands - a permanently red gate only
#                 trains people to bypass it (L22).
# ARMING: this list may legitimately run ahead of the fleet. The update-guard
# passes in total silence until $FM_HOME/state/.tor-update-scharf exists, so a
# row can be written the moment its target is agreed and becomes enforceable when
# the fleet arms the gate - no half-enforced middle state, and no window in which
# a not-yet-wired row blocks every update.
# ADDING A ROW: only for something whose absence actually disarms the fleet -
# a gate, a hook registration, the rule database, the rule CLI. Ordinary source
# files do not belong here; the guard is not a file census.
